ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows parallelogram ABCD with AB as the lower horizontal side labeled 16, BC as the right slanted side labeled 10, and DC as the upper horizontal side. The segment CD is extended left past D to E, with ED labeled 4, so E, D, C are collinear. The line BE crosses the slanted side AD at F. Since ED lies on the same horizontal line as CD, and CD is parallel to AB in the parallelogram, ED is parallel to AB. Reasoning: In parallelogram ABCD, opposite sides are equal, so AD = BC = 10. Consider triangle ABE. Since ED is parallel to AB, and F lies on both BE and AD, triangles EFD and BFA are similar. Therefore FD/FA = ED/AB = 4/16 = 1/4. Thus FA = 4FD. Because F lies on AD, AF + FD = AD = 10. Substituting gives 4FD + FD = 10, so 5FD = 10 and FD = 2.

method.method_draft: Use analytic coordinates/vectors. Place A=(0,0) and B=(16,0). From the text and diagram, take BC of length 10 making a 120 degree angle with BA, so in the displayed orientation BC=(5,5sqrt(3)). Then D=A+BC=(5,5sqrt(3)) and C=B+BC=(21,5sqrt(3)). Since CD is horizontal and DE=4 extends past D away from C, E=(1,5sqrt(3)). Parametrize AD by A+s(D-A)=(5s,5sqrt(3)s), and parametrize BE by B+t(E-B)=(16-15t,5sqrt(3)t). At the intersection F, equate coordinates: s=t from y-coordinates and 5s=16-15s from x-coordinates, so s=4/5. Since AD=10, FD=(1-s)AD=(1/5)10=2.
